# System Settings+ — the settings catalogue

<!-- Generated by scripts/settings-catalog-doc.ts from core/settings-catalog. Do not edit by hand. -->

Keeper by Ashforde® can read and change 397 system settings that usually need a terminal command or a buried switch
(137 on macOS, 133 on Windows, 127 on Linux). Open **System → System Settings+**, or type a setting's name in the
command palette.

## How it stays safe

- **Only catalogue operations run.** Each entry describes one operation (a `defaults` key, a registry value, a `gsettings` key,
  a `sysctl`, a service, a power setting…). Keeper builds the command from the entry as an argument list — never a shell line
  typed into the interface — and checks the value first (toggles and choices must be one of the listed values; numbers have
  limits; text cannot contain shell characters).
- **Exact preview.** Before anything changes you see the exact command(s), whether the administrator password is needed and
  what has to restart.
- **Backup first.** Before Keeper first changes an area each day it saves a snapshot: `defaults export` (macOS),
  `reg export` (Windows), `gsettings list-recursively` (Linux). *Backups* lists them with one-click restore.
- **Change log with undo.** Every change (by you, a profile or an AI agent you allowed) is logged with the previous value; *Undo*
  puts it back (or removes Keeper's value so the system default applies).
- **Administrator changes** go through the system's own prompt once per change (pkexec, the macOS password dialog, UAC). Kernel
  parameters are kept in Keeper's own `/etc/sysctl.d/99-keeper.conf`.
- **Advice entries** (GRUB, fstab, hosts, swap…) are explained with steps; Keeper reads them but never edits those files.
- **Setup profiles** export the settings you changed to a JSON file; importing shows a preview (what changes, what is already the
  same, what is for another system) and applies only what you tick.
- **AI agents** can search the catalogue (`system_settings_search`, allowed by default) and change a setting
  (`system_settings_change`, asks every time by default) — permissions in Settings → Abilities. Agent changes are logged and
  can be undone. The `keeper settings` command uses the same checks.

## Per-app controls

On every app in **App controls**, Applications, Processes and Network Activity (“App settings”).

| Control | macOS | Windows | Linux | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Network access**<br>Allow or block this app from the internet (a firewall rule). | yes | yes | yes | *Linux:* A rule in Keeper's firewall; how it is enforced on Linux (OpenSnitch or nftables) is shown on the Firewall page. |
| **Bandwidth limit**<br>Cap how fast this app can upload. | partial | yes | yes | *Windows:* Windows QoS policy by program name; limits sending (upload) only.<br>*Linux:* cgroup + nftables mark + tc HTB; limits sending (upload) only.<br>*macOS:* macOS has no per-app shaping: Keeper limits by the ports the app uses (pf + dummynet), which also affects other apps on those ports. |
| **Route through VPN**<br>Send this app through the VPN, or around it (split tunnelling). | guide | guide | yes | *Linux:* cgroup + firewall mark + a routing rule.<br>*Windows:* Windows has no per-app routing; use your VPN app's split tunnelling (WireGuard: AllowedIPs; many VPN apps have an app list).<br>*macOS:* macOS only allows per-app VPN with MDM profiles; use your VPN app's split tunnelling. |
| **DNS filter exception**<br>Let this app skip Keeper's DNS blocklists. | no | no | no | *macOS:* Not possible yet: Keeper's DNS filter sees each lookup but not which app made it. Pause the blocklist for a site in the Firewall page instead.<br>*Windows:* Not possible yet: Keeper's DNS filter sees each lookup but not which app made it. Pause the blocklist for a site in the Firewall page instead.<br>*Linux:* Not possible yet: Keeper's DNS filter sees each lookup but not which app made it. Pause the blocklist for a site in the Firewall page instead. |
| **Camera, microphone and location**<br>Which sensitive things this app may use. | guide | partial | partial | *macOS:* macOS only lets you grant these in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security; Keeper can reset an app's answers (tccutil reset).<br>*Windows:* Per-app switches for Store apps; desktop apps share one switch.<br>*Linux:* Flatpak apps: flatpak permission-set. Other apps are not sandboxed. |
| **CPU priority**<br>Give this app more or less of the processor when it is busy. | yes | yes | yes | *macOS:* renice, plus taskpolicy for background mode (efficiency cores on Apple silicon).<br>*Linux:* Raising priority above normal needs an administrator. |
| **CPU limit**<br>Never let this app use more than a share of the processor. | partial | yes | yes | *Windows:* A job object with a CPU rate cap.<br>*Linux:* cgroup v2 cpu.max.<br>*macOS:* macOS has no hard limit; Keeper can put the app in background mode (taskpolicy -b), which slows it down a lot when other work is waiting. |
| **Memory limit**<br>Stop this app growing past a size. | no | yes | yes | *macOS:* Not possible on macOS for normal apps.<br>*Windows:* Job object memory limit: the app is told it is out of memory past the limit.<br>*Linux:* cgroup v2 memory.max: the kernel reclaims memory, then stops the app if it goes past. |
| **Pause and resume**<br>Freeze the app completely (it uses no CPU) and wake it later. | yes | yes | yes |  |
| **Pause in the background**<br>Pause the app a few minutes after you switch away from it, resume when you come back. | yes | no | no | *Windows:* Not yet: Keeper hears which app is in front only on macOS. Use Pause and resume.<br>*Linux:* Not yet: Keeper hears which app is in front only on macOS (Wayland does not tell other apps). Use Pause and resume. |
| **Start at login**<br>Open this app when you sign in. | yes | yes | yes |  |
| **Notifications**<br>Allow or silence this app's notifications. | guide | yes | yes | *macOS:* macOS keeps notification permissions private; Keeper opens the right page in System Settings.<br>*Windows:* Uses the app's AppUserModelID; desktop apps without one cannot be switched individually.<br>*Linux:* GNOME per-app notification settings. |
| **Always light**<br>Keep this app light even when the system is dark. | yes | no | partial | *Windows:* Windows has no per-app override.<br>*Linux:* GTK apps: Keeper can start the app with GTK_THEME=Adwaita:light from its launcher. |
| **App language**<br>Use a different language in this app only. | yes | no | partial | *Windows:* Windows has no per-app language for desktop apps.<br>*Linux:* Keeper can start the app with LANGUAGE set from its launcher. |
| **App volume**<br>Set this app's volume separately. | no | yes | yes | *macOS:* macOS has no per-app volume without installing an audio driver; Keeper does not install one.<br>*Windows:* Core Audio session volume.<br>*Linux:* PipeWire / PulseAudio stream volume (pactl). |
| **Graphics card**<br>Run this app on the power-saving or high-performance graphics. | no | yes | partial | *macOS:* macOS chooses automatically.<br>*Linux:* Keeper can start the app with DRI_PRIME=1 / __NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1 from its launcher. |
| **Default app for file types**<br>Open these kinds of files with this app. | yes | guide | yes | *Windows:* Windows protects default-app choices; Keeper opens Settings ▸ Default apps at the right place. |

## Browser tab controls

Through Keeper's browser extension (`browser-extension/`) and the native messaging host (`keeper browser-host`). The
extension reports open tabs and what each page talks to; Keeper sends back checked commands (mute, sleep, close, site
permissions, blocking rules built from Keeper's enabled blocklists, clearing site data, per-site proxy as a PAC script). Data and
memory per tab are estimates (from response sizes). Nothing leaves the computer.

| Browser | What works |
|---|---|
| Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera | Everything: tabs, mute, sleep, site permissions (camera, microphone, location, notifications, JavaScript, cookies), blocking rules and per-site proxy. |
| Firefox | Tabs, mute, sleep, blocking rules, cookies and per-site proxy. Firefox has no contentSettings API, so camera, microphone, location and JavaScript per site are changed in Firefox's own site settings (the padlock in the address bar). |
| Safari | Not linked yet. A Safari extension can only talk to an app it is packaged inside and must be built with Xcode and signed by Apple; scripts/build-safari-extension.sh makes the Xcode project from the same extension on a Mac, but Keeper does not ship it yet. |

## Sources

Every entry links its documentation in the app (Details ⓘ). The main references: [ss64 defaults](https://ss64.com/mac/defaults.html),
[macos-defaults.com](https://macos-defaults.com/), [ss64 pmset](https://ss64.com/mac/pmset.html), Microsoft Learn (reg, powercfg, sc, DISM, policy CSPs,
privacy endpoints), the [GNOME admin guide](https://help.gnome.org/admin/system-admin-guide/stable/dconf.html.en),
[kernel sysctl docs](https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/sysctl/index.html) and the [systemd manual](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemctl.html).
